newsitem.title: ITALY: Berlusconi graft trial restarts from scratch.
newsitem.headline: Berlusconi graft trial restarts from scratch.

text.p: The corruption trial of former prime minister Silvio Berlusconi started again from scratch on Wednesday under a new presiding judge after the previous year-long hearing was declared null and void.
Berlusconi denies charges that four companies within his Fininvest business empire paid bribes to tax inspectors between 1989 and 1991 to obtain favourable audits.
Of the 11 defendants, only one former tax police officer turned up at the Milan court to hear presiding judge Francesca Manca formally reopen proceedings.

The original trial which began on January 17 last year was scrapped last month when presiding judge Carlo Crivelli stepped down in a row over allegations of bias and all the 27 trial hearings held so far were declared null and void.
Berlusconi, who served as prime minister for seven months in 1994, is already on trial for corruption with disgraced former Socialist premier Bettino Craxi, who is in self-imposed exile in Tunisia.
A committal hearing is also under way in Milan to decide whether Berlusconi should stand trial for allegedly setting up an illegal slush fund when Fininvest bought the Medusa film company in 1988.
